input: hand has length n in [0,10000], with integer card values in [0,1000000000]. groupSize is an integer in [1,10000]. Empty hand is explicitly accepted as zero groups. return: Boolean indicating whether all card occurrences can be partitioned into groups of exactly groupSize consecutive integer values. Every occurrence is used once; duplicates may occupy different groups. Nondivisible total length returns false, and empty input returns true.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs, caller-owned containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. A private frequency map is reduced while processing a newly sorted Array of distinct keys. No input cards are sorted, removed or changed. No grouping plan is returned.
numeric: All counts stay in [0,n]. Each start+offset probe is at most 1000009999 and exact. Positive groupSize prevents division-by-zero in the length modulo. A subtraction occurs only after available >= remaining, so counts never become negative. Relational sorting returns only -1,0,1.
complexity: O(n+u+1) map/group operations for u distinct cards plus sorting: every successful inner iteration removes at least one remaining occurrence, so there are at most n such iterations and at most one failing lookup. JavaScript adds T_sort(u) time and O(u+S_sort(u)) map/key space, with runtime-dependent sort costs. Hash-map/set time assumes average O(1) operations and bounded key costs; adversarial collision guarantees are not claimed. Qualify the actual JavaScript runtime rather than assuming ECMAScript mandates universal constant-time map operations.
